subject.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)

question: Should OpenClaw accept this PR's new opt-in `agents.defaults.compaction.turnMaintenanceTaskTimeoutMs` knob and per-run fence as the canonical deferred turn-maintenance recovery path, or should the fix reuse an existing compaction safety-timeout contract instead?
rationale: Repository policy sets a high bar for new config/default surfaces and treats session-state fencing as compatibility-sensitive, while the code and proof are otherwise strong enough that the remaining blocker is owner intent rather than a mechanical fix.

options.title: Accept the opt-in knob
options.body: Merge this PR after owner approval, keeping the default disabled so upgrades do not force-cancel existing long-running background engines.

options.title: Prefer the existing safety timeout
options.body: Pause or close this PR in favor of a proof-positive implementation that reuses the existing compaction timeout policy and avoids a new config key.

options.title: Request a narrower revision
options.body: Ask the contributor to remove or reshape the config surface while preserving the tested lane-release and late-side-effect fence behavior.

recommendation.title: Accept the opt-in knob
recommendation.body: Merge this PR after owner approval, keeping the default disabled so upgrades do not force-cancel existing long-running background engines.

likelyOwner.reason: jalehman merged and finalized the original background turn-maintenance task-routing feature, so this product/API choice is closest to that ownership trail.
